approach: Fault: StateDir::clean_job (state.rs) discards both the removal error and the size, so cleanup is silent and unmeasurable. Change it to return a CleanReport {bytes, error}; measure the tree size before pin::remove_tree. Add one helper (in state.rs) that each of the five call sites uses after its closing commit succeeds: it calls clean_job and emits a ui line 'reclaimed 11.4 GB' (human units) or 'warning: could not remove <path>: <err>'. Nothing to remove prints nothing and is not a failure. Call sites: manage.rs 135 (closed while blocked) and 224 (dropped/declined/interrupted-abandoned), run.rs 2276, 2451 (non-blocked only) and 2568 (retry landing). Cleanup stays after the commit, so running or blocked jobs keep their directory. Shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR is not adopted; the evidence goes in docs/decisions.md and athena.toml is left as is.

decisions.choice: Keep per-job target directories; delete them on close and report bytes reclaimed.
decisions.reason: Review 2 R14 showed a shared target dir ran another job's stale test binaries; per-job isolation (D46) is what the checks need. Deleting on close removes the disk growth without weakening checks.

rejected.why: Reuses another job's stale test binaries (R14); out of scope; concurrent jobs would also contend for the cargo build lock.

rejected.option: Sweep that deletes caches of already-closed historical jobs
rejected.why: Operational action on this machine, out of scope.

decisions.choice: clean_job returns a report (bytes, optional error with path) and the caller prints one ui line.
decisions.reason: One place measures and formats, so all closing paths report the same way; errors surface as a warning naming the path instead of being swallowed. The closing itself still succeeds, since the commit is already made.

rejected.option: Make removal failure fail the close
rejected.why: The records are already committed; failing would make the job look unclosed.

rejected.option: Add a reclaimed field to Closed/Finished structs
rejected.why: Wider change across consumers; a ui line meets the criterion.

decisions.choice: Human-unit formatting helper (decimal GB/MB/KB, one decimal) placed with the cleanup helper in state.rs, with display.rs only needing to render the line if the CLI's Ui wrapper formats lines.
decisions.reason: No existing byte formatter was found in the crates (grep), so add a small tested one.

rejected.option: Pull in a crate for byte formatting

steps: Change StateDir::clean_job to compute bytes (size walk) then call pin::remove_tree, returning CleanReport; add format_bytes and a report-to-ui helper; unit-test them.
Replace the five clean_job call sites in manage.rs and run.rs with the helper, keeping each after its commit and keeping the Blocked exception.
Adjust display.rs if closing lines are formatted there.
Add lifecycle.rs tests per closing path, removal failure (verified to succeed without injection as root) and kept-dir cases; fix any exact-output tests.
Write the decisions.md entry, CHANGELOG entry and README note; leave athena.toml unchanged.
Run cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, test.

risks.risk: Size walk is slow or miscounts symlinks/hard links on 12 GB trees.
risks.mitigation: Walk without following symlinks (symlink_metadata) and count file lengths; tests plant plain files.

risks.risk: A warning-only failure leaves a 12 GB directory.
risks.mitigation: Cleanup is best-effort and only warns; the commit is already made.

risks.risk: Existing tests that match exact closing output break.
risks.mitigation: Add a 'reclaimed' line only when bytes > 0, and update tests asserting exact output lines.

demonstrations.method: New tests in lifecycle.rs (and a unit test in state.rs) plant a target/ tree of known byte size in the job dir, close via landed, failed, rejected, abandoned, interrupted then `athena close`, and closed while blocked, then assert the dir is gone and the reclaimed count equals the planted size.
demonstrations.observes: All pass; job_dir absent and bytes equal the planted size for each path.
demonstrations.fails_without: If clean_job did not measure or if any path skipped cleanup, the directory would remain or the reported count would be 0 and the assertions would fail.

demonstrations.method: Tests capture the ui lines and assert one contains 'reclaimed 11.4 GB' for a planted ~11.4 GB sparse or scaled size via the formatter unit test, plus a no-cache job producing no warning/failure.
demonstrations.observes: Line text matches; no failure text when nothing to remove.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the formatted line the output assertion fails; with an empty job dir the test would show a spurious failure line.

demonstrations.method: Test makes removal fail (job dir path replaced so remove_tree errors, e.g. a path whose parent is not removable, run as root, so use an immutable or non-directory injection such as a regular file at a path that read_dir fails on). First show the same removal succeeds without the injection, then assert the warning names the path and the close still returns Ok.
demonstrations.observes: Warning line contains the job directory path.
demonstrations.fails_without: With errors swallowed, no warning line is emitted and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Tests: a blocked job after go (state Blocked) still has its job dir; a close whose commit is forced to fail (gate violation) leaves the dir intact.
demonstrations.fails_without: If cleanup ran before or regardless of commit success, the dir would be gone after a failed commit or while blocked.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff: a new decision entry with alternatives, citing athena-v0-review-2.md R14, and the decision not to share; athena.toml has no diff.
demonstrations.observes: Entry present with the evidence and decision; athena.toml unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks in turn: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked.
demonstrations.fails_without: Unformatted or lint-failing code would fail these.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff for a CHANGELOG entry stating that closing a job deletes its build cache and reports space reclaimed (and a README note).
demonstrations.observes: Entry present under the unreleased heading.

open_questions: Does the interrupted-job close path ever have the job dir locked or a running cargo? close_with checks the registry, so assumed safe.
Whether display.rs needs changes depends on how Ui lines are rendered; not read.
